literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该方法成功地重建了所有测试毒株的完整汉坦病毒基因组,并鉴定了高度丰富的缺陷病毒 基因组 (DVG) 和保守的 L 片段缺失,而 S 和 M 片段基本保持完整。 [10.64898/2026.10.19.760236]

在 47/137 个检测单位中检测到汉坦病毒RNA,其中包括 45 个阳性合并单位和两个单独的阳性样本。基于 343 只动物个体,描述性 MIR 为 13.7%,基于模型的个体水平感染概率估计为 18.0%(95% 概况似然 CI:13.5-23.1%)。在乌拉尔田鼠 (Apodemus uralensis)、银行田鼠 (Myodes glareolus) 和普通田鼠 (Microtus arvalis) 中观察到阳性检测单位。 [10.3390/zoonoticdis6040046]
基因组分析显示,测序病例中的病毒多样性有限,S 和 M 片段序列相同,且在 L 片段内仅检测到两个同义单核苷酸多态性 (SNP)。没有发现与增强传播性或持续人际传播相关的氨基酸变化的证据。暴发 序列与来自阿根廷的历史 ANDV 序列显示出大约 98.7% 的核苷酸同一性。 [PMCID:PMC13679879]
使用重组质粒标准品,在三个技术重复中以 1 × 10^1 拷贝/测试检测到两个目标;这是初步分析检测阈值,不包含提取损失或基质相关抑制。 [10.1016/j.jviromet.2026.115483]
对缺乏原钙粘蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 的人类细胞进行的基因研究表明,Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒利用 PCDH1 进行有效感染,尽管 Nova 表型较弱。除 Kenkeme 外,所有这些 Gn/Gc 蛋白均支持原代人内皮细胞的感染。 [10.1128/jvi.00994-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The method successfully reconstructed full hantavirus genomes across all tested strains and identified highly abundant defective viral genomes (DVGs) and conserved L segment deletions, while S and M segments remained largely intact. [10.64898/2026.10.19.760236]

Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%, and the model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). [10.3390/zoonoticdis6040046]

Genomic analyses revealed limited viral diversity among the sequenced cases, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment. [PMCID:PMC13679879]

Using recombinant plasmid standards, both targets were detected at 1 × 10^1 copies/test in three technical replicates; this is a preliminary analytical detection threshold and does not incorporate extraction losses or matrix-associated inhibition. [10.1016/j.jviromet.2026.115483]

Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells. [10.1128/jvi.00994-26]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 游轮上发生疑似汉坦病毒 暴发事件,已确认3人死亡,1人在重症监护室。世界卫生组织(WHO)确认了两例病例,报告了五例疑似病例,调查和进一步实验室检测仍在进行中。 [news-581d7186ba80cfda]
研究人员使用冷冻电镜和人工智能设计的支架来揭示安第斯病毒如何与人类受体 PCDH1 结合。他们还展示了抗体如何干扰这一过程。 [news-028d51ed44029480]
对汉坦病毒受体识别的结构和功能研究表明,安第斯病毒刺突使用四种糖蛋白形成一个深层中央口袋,用于捕获原钙粘蛋白-1。这项研究由 Bioengineer.org 报道。 [news-17d9b43d81a7aa64]
路易斯安那州立大学什里夫波特健康中心的科学家们正在帮助回答有关安第斯山脉汉坦病毒如何感染人类的​​问题,此前一艘游轮上出现了致命的 暴发。该事件被确认与汉坦病毒研究有关。 [news-df74452fb85457df]
MV Hondius 上疑似 暴发 的汉坦病毒导致乘客中 3 人死亡和数人患病。这一事件由联邦陪审团报告并得到世界卫生组织(WHO)评估的证实。 [news-3b472c5184e28b38]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hantaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: A suspected hantavirus outbreak occurred aboard the cruise ship, with three confirmed deaths and one person in intensive care. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed two cases and reported five suspected cases, with ongoing investigations and further laboratory testing. [news-581d7186ba80cfda]
Researchers used cryo-EM and AI-designed scaffolds to reveal how Andes virus binds to the human receptor PCDH1. They also showed how antibodies interfere with this process. [news-028d51ed44029480]

A structural and functional study of hantavirus receptor recognition revealed that the Andes virus spike uses four glycoproteins to form a deep central pocket that captures protocadherin-1. This study was reported by Bioengineer.org. [news-17d9b43d81a7aa64]

LSU Health Shreveport scientists are helping to answer questions about how the Andes hantavirus infects people, following a deadly outbreak on a cruise ship. The event is confirmed as related to hantavirus research. [news-df74452fb85457df]

A suspected outbreak of hantavirus on the MV Hondius resulted in three deaths and several illnesses among passengers. This event was reported by the federal jury and corroborated by the World Health Organization (WHO) assessment. [news-3b472c5184e28b38]

papers.title: Development of a rapid RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay for dual detection of Hantaan virus and Seoul virus.
papers.abstract: Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) are the primary causative agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), presenting a persistent challenge to global public health. Prompt and precise diagnostic tools are essential for clinical investigation and the containment of HFRS outbreaks. Leveraging the programmable precision of CRISPR/Cas12b system, which has significantly advanced the field of molecular diagnostics, we developed a rapid, high-sensitivity assay for the dual detection of HTNV and SEOV. Each virus was detected in a separate, target-specific single-tube reaction. The assay combines recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with CRISPR/Cas12b-mediated fluorescence detection and uses virus-specific sgRNAs and RPA primers targeting conserved genomic regions. Using recombinant plasmid standards, both targets were detected at 1 × 10 1 copies/test in three technical replicates; this is a preliminary analytical detection threshold and does not incorporate extraction losses or matrix-associated inhibition. No cross-reactivity was observed within the evaluated four-organism non-target panel. In a preliminary feasibility assessment, all nine RT-qPCR-positive rodent samples (seven HTNV and two SEOV) were positive by the RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay, indicating complete positive agreement in this all-positive sample set. Because no negative samples were included, negative agreement, diagnostic specificity, false-positive rate, and overall clinical diagnostic accuracy could not be assessed. These results support further development of the assay as a potential screening tool; larger studies using well-characterized positive and negative clinical or field specimens are required.

papers.title: An ONT sequencing framework for hantavirus genome assembly, variant analysis, and defective viral genome characterization from whole-segment amplicons
papers.abstract: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses that can cause severe human disease, necessitating improved methods for genome assembly and variant analysis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a sequencing framework using Oxford Nanopore Technologies to sequence hantavirus genomes from whole-segment amplicons, applied to diverse Puumala virus strains, Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo.
analysis.methods: The framework uses universal reverse transcription primers targeting conserved genome termini and species-specific primer pairs per segment, combined with a bioinformatic pipeline for reference-guided assembly, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification.
analysis.main_results: The method successfully reconstructed full hantavirus genomes across all tested strains and identified highly abundant defective viral genomes (DVGs) and conserved L segment deletions, while S and M segments remained largely intact.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations, highlighting the importance of this framework for understanding viral diversity and genome instability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This framework provides a low-cost, broadly applicable workflow for hantavirus genomics, which can improve surveillance, diagnosis, and understanding of viral evolution and pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches fail to capture virus population heterogeneity, including DVGs, but the study demonstrates accurate genome reconstruction using its novel method, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework tailored for hantavirus genome assembly and variant analysis. The framework utilizes universal reverse transcription primers and species-specific primer pairs to amplify and sequence complete S, M, and L segments, along with a bioinformatic pipeline for reference-guided assembly and DVG classification. Applied to diverse hantavirus strains, including Puumala virus, Old World, and New World orthohantaviruses, the method accurately reconstructed full genomes and identified abundant defective viral genomes (DVGs) and conserved L segment deletions. These findings reveal DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations, offering a low-cost, adaptable workflow for hantavirus genomics. The study highlights the limitations of existing methods in capturing viral heterogeneity but demonstrates the effectiveness of its approach in reconstructing genomes, providing moderate confidence in its utility for surveillance and understanding viral evolution.

papers.title: Hantavirus RNA Detection in Small Mammals and Spatial Comparison with Reported Human HFRS Cases in West Kazakhstan Region, 2025
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compare rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. This addresses the need to understand the role of small mammals in the transmission of hantaviruses and the potential for human infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts of the West Kazakhstan Region, involving the capture and morphological identification of 343 small mammals.
analysis.methods: Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Real-time and conventional RT-PCR were used to evaluate 137 testing units representing 343 animals. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size.
analysis.main_results: Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%, and the model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found a significant presence of hantavirus RNA in small mammals, with a higher infection rate than previously reported. This suggests a potential risk of hantavirus transmission to humans, particularly in areas where human HFRS cases have been reported.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against the potential for hantavirus transmission from small mammals to humans, especially in areas with overlapping settlements and reported human HFRS cases. This has implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and the use of pooled testing, which may underestimate the true infection rate. The sample size and geographical coverage are also limited, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study detected hantavirus RNA in small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region, with a higher infection rate than previously reported. The findings suggest a potential risk of hantavirus transmission to humans, particularly in areas with overlapping settlements and reported human HFRS cases, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance and prevention strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 2025 年西哈萨克斯坦地区小型哺乳动物中汉坦病毒RNA 的检测和空间分布,并将啮齿动物 监测 的发现与人类 HFRS 的发生率进行比较。这解决了了解小型哺乳动物在 传播 和汉坦病毒中的作用以及人类感染的可能性的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年 7 月和 9 月在西哈萨克斯坦地区的四个地区进行了一项观察性横断面分析研究,涉及 343 种小型哺乳动物的捕获和形态鉴定。
elements_zh.methods: 9 月份收集的 329 只动物的肺组织样本在 123 个混合测试单位进行了检查,而 7 月份收集的 14 只动物进行了单独测试。使用实时和常规 RT-PCR 评估代表 343 只动物的 137 个测试单位。最小感染率(MIR)被计算为描述性估计,并使用合并测试似然模型来解释测试单元大小的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 47/137 个检测单位中检测到汉坦病毒RNA,其中包括 45 个阳性合并单位和两个单独的阳性样本。基于 343 只动物个体,描述性 MIR 为 13.7%,基于模型的个体水平感染概率估计为 18.0%(95% 概况似然 CI:13.5-23.1%)。在乌拉尔田鼠 (Apodemus uralensis)、银行田鼠 (Myodes glareolus) 和普通田鼠 (Microtus arvalis) 中观察到阳性检测单位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现小型哺乳动物体内大量存在汉坦病毒RNA,其感染率比之前报道的要高。这表明汉坦病毒传播 对人类存在潜在风险,特别是在已报告人类 HFRS 病例的地区。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compare rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. This addresses the need to understand the role of small mammals in the transmission of hantaviruses and the potential for human infection.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts of the West Kazakhstan Region, involving the capture and morphological identification of 343 small mammals.
analysis_en.methods: Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Real-time and conventional RT-PCR were used to evaluate 137 testing units representing 343 animals. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size.
analysis_en.main_results: Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%, and the model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found a significant presence of hantavirus RNA in small mammals, with a higher infection rate than previously reported. This suggests a potential risk of hantavirus transmission to humans, particularly in areas where human HFRS cases have been reported.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against the potential for hantavirus transmission from small mammals to humans, especially in areas with overlapping settlements and reported human HFRS cases. This has implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and the use of pooled testing, which may underestimate the true infection rate. The sample size and geographical coverage are also limited, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 2025 年西哈萨克斯坦地区小型哺乳动物中的 RNA 检测以及与报告的人类 HFRS 病例的空间比较
papers.source_body_en: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.
papers.abstract_zh: 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 是一种与天然啮齿动物 宿主 中的正汉坦病毒相关的人畜共患疾病。本研究评估了 2025 年西哈萨克斯坦地区小型哺乳动物中汉坦病毒RNA 的检测和空间分布,并将啮齿动物 监测 的发现与人类 HFRS 的发生率进行了比较。2025 年 7 月和 9 月在四个地区进行了一项观察性横断面分析研究。共捕获并鉴定小型哺乳动物343只。9 月份收集的 329 只动物的肺组织样本在 123 个混合测试单位进行了检查,而 7 月份收集的 14 只动物进行了单独测试。因此,通过实时和常规 RT-PCR 评估了代表 343 只动物的 137 个测试单位。最小感染率(MIR)被计算为描述性最小估计值,并使用合并测试似然模型来解释测试单元大小的变化。在 47/137 个检测单位中检测到汉坦病毒RNA,其中包括 45 个阳性合并单位和两个单独的阳性样本。基于 343 只动物个体,描述性 MIR 为 13.7%。基于模型的个体水平感染概率估计为 18.0%(95% 轮廓似然 CI:13.5-23.1%)。在乌拉尔田鼠 (Apodemus uralensis)、银行田鼠 (Myodes glareolus) 和普通田鼠 (Microtus arvalis) 中观察到阳性检测单位。在地区一级,描述性 MIR 范围从布尔林斯基的 11.6% 到钦吉尔劳伊斯基的 19.0%。采样点与报告人类 HFRS 病例的定居点在空间上重叠,包括 Utvinka、Daryinsk 和 Rubezhinskoye;然而,空间重合并不能建立直接的传播。

papers.title: Can Hantavirus cruise into the next pandemic?
papers.abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.

papers.full_text: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness. Could ANDV cause a future pandemic?Despite documented person-to-person transmission associated with the M/V Hondius cluster, current epidemiological and genomic evidence indicates that the likelihood of this outbreak progressing to sustained epidemic or pandemic transmission was exceedingly low. Prompt implementation of public health interventions, including quarantine measures and active surveillance of individuals aboard the vessel, facilitated the early identification and isolation of suspected cases. Furthermore, genomic analyses revealed remarkably limited viral diversity among sequenced cases from the M/V Hondius cluster, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment, one in case 5 and another in case 7. Importantly, no evidence of amino acid changes associated with enhanced transmissibility or sustained human-to-human spread was identified.18 In contrast, the outbreak sequences showed approximately 98.7% nucleotide identity across all three genome segments with ANDV sequences identified in Argentina in 1997 and 2018, indicating considerably greater divergence from these historical reference sequences.18 Furthermore, the reported positive cases fell within the incubation period of nine to 45 days for ANDV, suggesting that the cluster may have originated from a limited zoonotic exposure event, potentially followed by restricted secondary transmission, and is unlikely to develop into an epidemic or a pandemic event. However, given that ANDV has historically caused multiple outbreaks, it is important to highlight the conditions that could enable localised ANDV outbreaks to evolve and escalate into larger epidemics, and potentially, under exceptional circumstances, into a pandemic threat among human populations, as illustrated in Figure.Figure:Potential drivers of Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak escalation and pandemic emergence. ANDV is maintained in rodent reservoirs, primarily the long-tailed pygmy rice rat (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus), and is transmitted to humans through inhalation of aerosolised rodent excreta. Unlike other orthohantaviruses, ANDV can also undergo limited person-to-person transmission, although sustained community transmission has not been documented. The graphical abstract highlights three factors that could contribute to outbreak escalation: (i) viral evolution through mutation, reassortment, and host adaptation; (ii) environmental and ecological changes that increase rodent abundance and spillover risk; and (iii) expansion of reservoir host range through host switching and reservoir diversification. Under favourable ecological and evolutionary conditions, these processes could increase the scale, frequency, geographic distribution, or transmission potential of future outbreaks, underscoring the importance of continued surveillance, preparedness, and the development of effective diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. Illustration created with BioRender.com.First - The acquisition of beneficial mutations may facilitate adaptation to human hosts. Genetic variation arising during viral replication could theoretically influence viral fitness, host range, or transmission efficiency under selective pressures. Orthohantaviruses replicate using an error-prone RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), with evolutionary rates estimated at approximately 10−2-10−4 substitutions per site per year, consistent with rates reported for other RNA viruses.19 However, the relationship between genomic variation and altered transmissibility in ANDV remains incompletely understood, and no specific adaptive mutations have yet been conclusively associated with sustained human-to-human transmission.Previous studies have shown that ANDV strains from rodent and human hosts can produce markedly different outcomes in the Syrian hamster model.2021 Notably, a Chilean human isolate (CHI-7913), recovered from a fatal HPS case, acquired only a single non-synonymous mutation after 25 serial passages in hamsters and remained non-pathogenic, indicating relative genomic stability.20 In contrast, the rodent-derived isolate Chile-9717869 causes uniformly lethal disease despite differing by 23 amino acids from CHI-7913.21 Although these findings suggest a degree of genomic stability, they do not necessarily preclude adaptation. One possible explanation is that the CHI-7913 isolate had already undergone host-specific adaptation following zoonotic transmission to humans, thereby enhancing fitness in human cells while reducing replication efficiency and pathogenicity in the Syrian hamster model. Collectively, these observations indicate that relatively few genetic changes can substantially alter host adaptation and disease phenotype in ANDV, while the molecular determinants governing virulence and transmissibility remain incompletely understood.Several biological mechanisms may contribute to these processes, including alterations in receptor usage, interferon antagonism, and genome reassortment. Pathogenic orthohantaviruses utilise β3 integrins, protocadherin-1, and other endothelium-associated receptors for host-cell entry, and mutations affecting glycoprotein-receptor interactions could alter host permissiveness and enhance adaptation to humans.2223242526 In addition, the ability of orthohantaviruses to suppress interferon signalling contributes to reservoir persistence and may influence pathogenicity across different hosts.2728293031 Importantly, the segmented orthohantavirus genome permits genetic reassortment during co-infection, potentially generating novel phenotypic combinations with altered virulence, transmissibility, or host range.32 Although reassortment appears less frequent than in other members of the order Bunyavirales (e.g. orthobunyaviruses) and influenza viruses, it remains an important mechanism contributing to long-term evolutionary adaptation and host expansion.33Second - An increase in rodent reservoir populations driven by environmental and ecological changes may amplify the risk of zoonotic spillover. Environmental disruption is a well-recognised determinant of orthohantavirus emergence and transmission dynamics.3435 Climatic oscillations, including El Niño-associated rainfall patterns, can substantially increase rodent abundance and population density, thereby elevating opportunities for human exposure, as previously documented during Sin Nombre virus (SNV) outbreaks in North America. In South America, deforestation, agricultural expansion, urban encroachment into rural and forested ecosystems, and biodiversity disturbance may similarly intensify contact between humans and ANDV reservoir hosts. In parallel, globalisation and expanding transportation networks have facilitated the international dissemination of rodent-associated orthohantaviruses, as illustrated by the spread of Seoul virus (SEOV) through maritime trade and the pet rat industry.36 Collectively, these ecological and anthropogenic pressures may increase the frequency of spillover events and the geographic distribution of orthohantavirus exposure. However, there is currently no evidence that such conditions alone are sufficient to drive sustained human-to-human transmission or pandemic-level spread of ANDV.Third - Expansion of reservoir host range may contribute to broader geographic dissemination and increased opportunities for human exposure. Orthohantaviruses were historically considered highly host-specific pathogens, with individual virus lineages predominantly associated with a single rodent reservoir species through long-term co-evolutionary relationships.3738 ANDV is primarily associated with Oligoryzomys longicaudatus as its principal reservoir host. However, accumulating phylogenetic and ecological evidence has challenged the concept of strict host specificity, demonstrating that host-switching events, spillover infections, and reservoir diversification have likely occurred repeatedly throughout orthohantavirus evolutionary history.193940 In addition, the identification of genetically divergent orthohantaviruses in shrews, moles, and bats suggests that ancestral orthohantaviruses may have undergone multiple historical cross-species transmission events.394142 Collectively, these findings indicate that orthohantavirus host associations, although generally stable, are not biologically absolute. Habitat disruptions, altered species interactions, and environmental pressures could therefore increase opportunities for cross-species transmission and geographic expansion over extended ecological timescales, potentially increasing the frequency of human exposure to infected reservoir hosts. Nevertheless, there is currently no evidence that such ecological processes have resulted in ANDV lineages with enhanced sustained human-to-human transmissibility. Current preparedness against ANDV outbreaksPerhaps more worrying is the limited availability of rapid diagnostics, antivirals, and vaccines for responding to outbreaks of ANDV and other clinically relevant orthohantaviruses. Several antiviral and immunotherapeutic strategies have been explored against human disease-causing orthohantaviruses, including nucleoside analogues such as ribavirin, favipiravir and ETAR; entry inhibitors such as lactoferrin and griffithsin; host-directed approaches targeting vascular leakage pathways; RNAi-based strategies; and, more recently, neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting the Gn/Gc glycoprotein complex.(2,3,43-48) However, no orthohantavirus-specific antiviral has yet become an established standard of care, and most candidates remain experimental or dependent on very early administration. In parallel, vaccine development efforts have advanced substantially over the past decades. Hantavax®, an inactivated orthohantavirus vaccine marketed in South Korea to prevent HFRS caused by Hantaan and Seoul viruses, remains among the only orthohantavirus vaccines licensed for human use, while several next-generation vaccine candidates are currently under development and evaluation in preclinical and early-phase clinical trials.4349 Despite these advances, effective countermeasures specifically targeting ANDV remain limited, highlighting an important preparedness gap for future outbreaks.In conclusion - Overall, current evidence does not support the conclusion that ANDV is imminently poised to emerge as a pandemic pathogen comparable to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Nevertheless, under favourable ecological and epidemiological conditions, localised ANDV outbreaks may increase in scale or geographic distribution, potentially posing broader regional public health challenges. These considerations underscore the importance of strengthening preparedness strategies to prevent the escalation of orthohantavirus outbreaks, particularly in under-resourced endemic regions of South America. Integrated ecological surveillance approaches, including climate-informed forecasting of rodent population dynamics,50 together with genomic epidemiological surveillance of ANDV and other clinically relevant orthohantaviruses, may improve early detection of spillover risk, characterise orthohantavirus diversity and evolutionary dynamics, and support timely public health responses. In addition, expanded availability of antiviral therapeutics, monoclonal antibodies, preventive vaccines, and rapid diagnostic platforms will be important for comprehensive orthohantavirus outbreak preparedness and response. These diagnostic platforms could include lateral-flow assays to detect orthohantavirus-specific IgM and IgG antibodies in symptomatic patients,51 as well as antigen-based tests for direct virus detection in both humans and reservoir hosts. REVIEWER #1The manuscript titled “Could Hantavirus Transmit the Next Pandemic?” presents a compelling and relevant discussion regarding the potential for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) outbreaks. Prompted by the recent atypical HCPS outbreak associated with Andes orthohantavirus (ANDV) aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius, the authors analyze this threat from virological, genomic, and eco-epidemiological perspectives. They convincingly argue that sustained person-to-person transmission would require highly specific—and currently unlikely—evolutionary conditions.The manuscript, from the abstract to the main text and references, is clear and well-structured. Notably, the authors present robust evidence that ANDV currently lacks the adaptive mutations necessary to drive person-to-person transmission in the manner observed with influenza viruses or SARS-CoV-2. This provides a timely and necessary clarification: although hantaviruses possess a trisegmented RNA genome capable of rapid mutation, reassortment and host adaptation, a large-scale epidemic remains highly unlikely. Finally, by advocating for an integrated global approach—combining genomic-epidemiological monitoring, rapid diagnostics, and accessible therapies—the authors highlight the precise surveillance strategies needed to contain localized HCPS outbreaks before they escalate into regional public health threats. Thus, in addition to adequately answering the title’s central question, the authors highlight the urgent global need for continuous, targeted surveillance—adopting a One Health approach—in areas endemic for SCPH, as well as for the accelerated development of effective diagnostics, specific therapies, and vaccines against HCPS.Minor comments: (i) standardized taxonomy — replace the word “hantavirus” with “orthohantavirus”, and (ii) in the graphical abstract : Oligoryzomys longicaudatus has been correctly italicized and change “exposure to aerosolised” to “inhalation of aerosolized.” REVIEWER #2This manuscript presents an interesting ecoevolutionary perspective into the outstanding question of Hantavirus’ pandemic potential. It has been discussed long before the Hondius outbreak that hantaviruses are worth being surveilled and studied to better understand if through evolution and expansion of host distributions and rodent-human contact interfaces, Hantaviruses could become the agents behind the next pandemic. The authors create a solid compendium of evidence regarding these scenarios and provide a grounded commentary on ANDV’s lack of pandemic potential at the moment, bringing a sobering message at a time when the lay public needs a better understanding of Hantaviruses.That being said, I would like to suggest some minor changes to enhance the flow of the manuscript:1. In the background section, there should be 2-3 sentences introducing the reader to the M/V Hondius situation. At the time of this review, the Hondius is not at the front page of the news anymore, and moreover, the manuscript should be timeless. For that reason, it would be good if the authors could include a section explaining the Hondius outbreak.2. Related to the first point, in lines 64-66, the authors dive right into discussing the “likelihood that the M/V Hondius ANDV cluster could progress into a sustained epidemic”. Before this section, there is no context of what the N/V Hondius ANDV cluster is.3. In lines 69-70, the authors mention that the sequences derived from the ANDV cluster have two synonymous mutations with respect to ANDV reference sequences from Argentina (1997 and 2018) and cite the Virological.org post by Dr. Gustavo Palacios. However, that is not what the post mentions; instead, the post describes two nonsynonymous mutations arising in the L segment between the first three sequences generated in South Africa, and they argue that this is a sign of a single spillover event as the origin of the index case. The original publication then mentions “98.76% and 98.75% based on the L segment, 98.71% and 98.68% on the M segment and 98.73% and 98.73% on the S segment”, these are with respect to the reference sequences from 1997 and 2018, which is more than two SNPs. Therefore, the authors should rectify the assertion of only two SNPs in the Hondius sequences, it would be evolutionarily impossible for an RNA virus to only accumulate two mutations in almost 30 years. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the pandemic risk of Andes virus (ANDV) following a recent ship-associated outbreak, addressing concerns about its potential to cause widespread transmission. The background highlights the need to evaluate whether documented person-to-person transmission could lead to sustained epidemic or pandemic spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed a ship-associated outbreak of ANDV, focusing on the M/V Hondius cruise. It included genomic analyses of sequenced cases and epidemiological data from the outbreak, with a sample size of seven confirmed cases.
analysis.methods: Genomic analyses were conducted on sequenced cases to assess viral diversity, while epidemiological data were used to evaluate the incubation period and transmission patterns. The study also examined the relationship between outbreak sequences and historical ANDV sequences from Argentina.
analysis.main_results: Genomic analyses revealed limited viral diversity among the sequenced cases, with identical S and M segment sequences and only two synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected within the L segment. No evidence of amino acid changes linked to enhanced transmissibility or sustained human-to-human spread was found. The outbreak sequences showed approximately 98.7% nucleotide identity with historical ANDV sequences from Argentina.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the likelihood of the outbreak progressing to sustained epidemic or pandemic transmission was exceedingly low, based on the limited viral diversity and absence of transmissibility-enhancing mutations. papers.title: Expanded protocadherin-1 usage reveals a broader hantavirus entry landscape
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity. IMPORTANCE Many newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity. IMPORTANCE Many newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 哺乳动物汉坦病毒是一种 RNA 病毒,在美洲引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征,在欧亚大陆引起 肾综合征出血热。大多数汉坦病毒的细胞进入机制仍然不明确。为了检查在非洲、欧亚大陆和美洲发现的系统发育上不同的汉坦病毒的条目,我们生成了具有复制能力的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV),其带有 Necoclí、Sangassou、Thottapalayam、Kenkeme、Nova、Oxbow 和 Tula 病毒的 Gn/Gc 蛋白。除 Kenkeme 外,所有这些 Gn/Gc 蛋白均支持原代人内皮细胞的感染,表明内皮细胞进入允许的汉坦病毒范围比之前认识的更广泛。除了 rVSV-Kenkeme 之外,这些 rVSV 在救援和传代过程中除了预先设计的救援增强变化外,没有获得额外的 突变。对缺乏原钙粘蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 的人类细胞进行的基因研究表明,Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒利用 PCDH1 进行有效感染,尽管 Nova 表型较弱。这三种Gn/Gc蛋白以不同的表观亲合力结合可溶性PCDH1,并且可溶性PCDH1抑制相应rVSV的感染;Necoclí 和 Tula(但不是 Nova)也被 PCDH1 靶向单克隆抗体阻断。在 PCDH1 敲除的内皮细胞中,真正的图拉病毒感染也同样减少。最后,具有广泛反应性的抗 Gn/Gc 人单克隆抗体 ADI-42898 可有效中和 Necoclí、Nova、Sangassou 和 Kenkeme rVSV,但对 Oxbow、Tula 和 Thottapalayam rVSV 的活性较弱或无法检测到。总之,这些发现扩大了能够介导人内皮细胞感染的汉坦病毒糖蛋白的范围,扩大了 PCDH1 依赖性进入的系统发育范围,并确定了具有不同活性的受体靶向和病毒糖蛋白靶向策略。重要性 许多新发现的汉坦病毒只能从序列数据中得知,因此它们进入人体细胞的能力及其受体的使用尚未解决。使用 BSL2 兼容的重组水泡性口炎病毒 (rVSV) 系统,我们发现来自几种不同汉坦病毒的糖蛋白可以介导原代人内皮细胞的感染,这表明内皮细胞进入的许可范围比之前预期的更广泛。我们还表明,原钙粘蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 以前主要与新世界汉坦病毒有关,被 Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒使用,但在整个组中并不普遍,揭示了更广泛但异质的受体使用。真实的图拉病毒实验在替代系统之外支持了这一结论。最后,一种具有广泛反应性的抗 Gn/Gc 抗体可以中和其中几种病毒,但不是全部,这凸显了广泛保护性对策的前景和局限性,以及这些 rVSV 在评估进入抑制剂方面的效用。

papers.title: Hantaviruses as Emerging Zoonotic Pathogens: Molecular Biology, Epidemiology, Therapeutics, vaccine, and Pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic pathogens belonging to the family Hantaviridae and are responsible for two major human diseases, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Despite substantial progress in hantavirus research, important challenges remain in understanding the interactions among viral evolution, reservoir ecology, environmental change, transmission dynamics, and host immunopathology. This review provides an integrated One Health perspective that connects molecular virology and host-virus interactions with transmission ecology, global epidemiology, and the mechanisms underlying vascular leakage and severe disease. papers.title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial–coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet–leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

papers.title: IDENTIFICATION OF A STRUCTURALLY AND EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED 3'→5' PROOFREADING EXONUCLEASE DOMAIN IN THE LARGE L PROTEIN OF HANTAVIRUSES- EMERGING HUMAN PATHOGENS
papers.abstract: The proofreading 3′→5′ exonuclease not only represents a crucial class of enzymes responsible for maintaining genome integrity across diverse groups of organisms, but also plays a critical role in ensuring replication fidelity. In the non-segmented, positive-strand bat-borne RNA viruses like Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronaviruses (SARS-CoVs and MERS-CoV), it is found along with the methyltransferase (MTase) gene of the non-structural protein 14 (NSP14). In contrast, in the non-segmented, but negative-strand bat-borne RNA viruses such as Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses, it has been identified together with a novel type of capping enzyme, viz. guanosine diphosphate polyribonucleotidyltransferase (PRNTase). Hantaviruses, one of the fatal and emerging human pathogens in recent times, belong to segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and are primarily rodent-borne. Currently, no universally approved vaccine or antiviral therapy exists for all hantavirus infections. The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been reported in hantaviruses until now. Interestingly, a putative PR exonuclease domain has been identified for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses. To the best of my knowledge, this study provides the first evidence for the presence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, and thus, expanding our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and further presenting a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify a structurally and evolutionarily conserved 3′→5′ proofreading exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, which are emerging human pathogens. The background highlights the importance of such enzymes in maintaining genome integrity and replication fidelity across various organisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on hantaviruses, which are segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses primarily rodent-borne. It examined the presence of a proofreading exonuclease domain in these viruses, specifically within the large L protein, and compared it with other RNA viruses.
analysis.methods: The researchers identified a putative PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses through sequence analysis and structural comparison. They compared this domain with those found in other RNA viruses, such as SARS-CoVs and MERS-CoV, and noted structural deviations in the catalytic triad and proton acceptor site.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been previously identified in hantaviruses. It was found for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the newly identified domain in hantaviruses belongs to the DEDD superfamily, similar to bacterial DNA polymerases and DNA viruses. This finding expands the understanding of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The discovery of a PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses presents a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on sequence analysis and structural comparison, which may not fully capture functional aspects. However, the evidence is strong as it provides the first report of a PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, supported by structural and comparative data.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies a structurally and evolutionarily conserved 3′→5′ proofreading exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, which are emerging human pathogens. The research highlights the absence of such a domain in hantaviruses until now and notes its presence in the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The domain is found to belong to the DEDD superfamily, similar to bacterial DNA polymerases and DNA viruses, and exhibits distinct structural features. This finding expands the understanding of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and presents a novel structural target for the development of antiviral therapies. The study's evidence is strong, as it provides the first report of this domain in hantaviruses, but it is limited to sequence and structural analysis without functional validation.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究的重点是 汉坦病毒,这是一种主要由啮齿动物传播的分段负链 RNA 病毒。它检查了这些病毒中是否存在校对核酸外切酶结构域,特别是在大 L 蛋白内,并将其与其他 RNA 病毒进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过序列分析和结构比较,在汉坦病毒中鉴定出了一个假定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域。他们将该结构域与其他 RNA 病毒(例如 SARS-CoV 和 MERS-CoV)中发现的结构域进行了比较,并注意到催化三联体和质子受体位点的结构偏差。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,此前尚未在汉坦病毒中鉴定出校对 (PR) 核酸外切酶结构域。它首次在这些病毒的大 L 蛋白中被发现,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 汉坦病毒 中 PR 核酸外切酶结构域的发现为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法提供了新的结构靶点。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于序列分析和结构比较,可能无法完全捕获功能方面。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它提供了汉坦病毒中 PR 核酸外切酶结构域的第一份报告,并有结构和比较数据的支持。

papers.title: Development of a One-Step RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b Assay for Rapid On-Site Detection of Dabie Bandavirus
papers.abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus (DBV), has rapidly spread to multiple countries worldwide since its discovery in 2009, posing a serious threat to global public health security. SFTS is a tick-borne disease, and people living in mountainous and hilly areas are at increased risk of infection, which highlights the urgent need for rapid, accurate, and field-applicable diagnostic strategies for DBV. In this study, LAMP primers and CRISPR sgRNA were designed based on the conserved region of the DBV L segment. A one-pot, one-step molecular assay integrating reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) with CRISPR/Cas12b technology was established after systematic optimization of key parameters. The assay operates under isothermal conditions at 60 °C, delivering results within 40 min. Analytical evaluation demonstrated a limit of detection of 25.6 RNA copies per reaction. No cross-reactivity was observed with Hantaan virus, Seoul virus, Chikungunya virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Dengue virus, and Zika virus. Clinical validation using 42 specimens showed complete concordance with gold-standard qRT-PCR, achieving 100% sensitivity (30/30) and 100% specificity (12/12). For point-of-care application, fluorescence visualization was incorporated into the CRISPR/Cas-based detection workflow, enabling straightforward result interpretation. This integrated RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b platform provides rapid and specific detection of DBV through a simplified workflow that does not require complex instrumentation, supporting its potential application in resource-limited environments.

papers.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike. The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

papers.title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), particularly those caused by hantaviruses, and aims to develop an integrated operational framework for emergency medical systems. The central question is how to safely move patients with hantavirus infections between different care settings while maintaining biosafety.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, incorporating guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and organized across seven operational domains, combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies, and the findings are primarily based on case reports and technical evaluations. There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions, and the framework components require prospective evaluation. Additionally, the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service is a key source of data, but this may not be representative of all emergency medical systems.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The framework proposed in the review is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance in biocontainment transport. It highlights the need for prospective evaluation of its components and emphasizes the importance of integrating operational experience into the development of emergency medical systems. The review also underscores the necessity for further research on the effectiveness of interventions and the development of standardized protocols for biocontainment transport.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review addresses the transport of patients with hantavirus infections, focusing on the integration of biosafety science and emergency medicine. It synthesizes the international literature on biocontainment transport and develops an operational framework for emergency medical systems. The review highlights recurrent findings such as device integrity, air quality, self-contamination risks, heat strain, communication challenges, and psychological burdens. It emphasizes the need for a structured, consensus-based approach and calls for prospective evaluation of the framework components. The review also identifies gaps in comparative studies and underscores the importance of operational experience in shaping best practices for biocontainment transport.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 此次审查的重点是严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的转运,特别是由汉坦病毒引起的患者,旨在制定紧急医疗系统的综合运作框架。核心问题是如何在不同护理环境之间安全转移汉坦病毒感染患者,同时保持生物安全。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索,纳入了世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。研究结果根据 SANRA 规模进行报告,并在七个业务领域进行组织,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 文献缺乏比较研究,研究结果主要基于病例报告和技术评估。关于具体干预措施有效性的证据有限,框架组成部分需要前瞻性评估。此外,审查指出,意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验是关键数据来源,但这可能无法代表所有紧急医疗系统。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查中提出的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的参考,用于生物防护运输的规划、培训和质量保证。它强调了对其组成部分进行前瞻性评估的必要性,并强调将运营经验融入紧急医疗系统开发的重要性。该审查还强调了进一步研究干预措施有效性和制定生物防护运输标准化方案的必要性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:严重传染病(HCID)患者的转运将生物安全科学和急诊医学联系在一起。2026年的本迪布焦病毒病疫情以及与一艘探险游轮相关的多国安第斯山脉病毒暴发再次引起人们对如何在社区、医院和高级隔离单位之间安全转移此类患者的关注。这篇叙述性综述综合了有关生物防护运输的国际文献,并将其整合到紧急医疗系统的操作框架中。方法:根据 SANRA 量表,对 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus(截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日)进行结构化检索,并辅以世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导。证据跨七个业务领域进行组织,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。结果:在已识别的 2432 条记录中,筛选出 1485 条独特记录。文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估和专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果涉及运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、个人防护设备造成的热应变和通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间团队准备状态的保持以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。结论:生物防护运输最好理解为一个综合应急系统,而不是一种以设备为中心的干预措施。拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考;其组成部分需要前瞻性评估。

OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM Share Follow ABC News on Google A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." Ilhan Omar says she will move from her Washington, DC, home after federal search 1 day ago Man hops onto moving school bus when he sees driver in distress 1 day ago Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Oct 16 WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus said in a post on X on Sunday that the organization is working closely with both member states and ship operators in response to the suspected hantavirus cases. "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC.
